title: WorldLines: Benchmarking and Modeling Long-Horizon Stateful Embodied Agents
abstract: arXiv:2606.18847v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: To assist humans over extended periods in real homes, embodied agents must remember user routines, world states, and past interactions. Existing long-term memory benchmarks mainly evaluate language-centric retrieval and question answering, while embodied benchmarks often focus on short-horizon task execution without testing long-term memory use in dynamic environments. We introduce WorldLines, a project-driven benchmark for long-horizon embodied household assistance. It constructs temporally extended household traces with dialogues, actions, execution feedback, object and device state changes, and converts them into evidence-linked samples for Memory QA and Embodied Task Planning. We further propose ObsMem, an observer-grounded memory framework that maintains visibility-aware memories and action-native state trails for state-aware decisions. Experiments reveal persistent challenges in partial observability, overwritten world states,

translated_title: WorldLines：基准测试与建模长期跨度的有状态具身智能体
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2606.18847v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：为了在真实家庭环境中长时间协助人类，具身智能体必须记住用户习惯、世界状态和过去的交互。现有的长期记忆基准主要评估以语言为中心的检索和问答，而具身基准通常侧重于短时程任务执行，未测试动态环境中长期记忆的使用。我们引入了WorldLines，一个项目驱动的基准测试，用于长期跨度的具身家庭辅助。它构建了时间上延伸的家庭轨迹，包含对话、动作、执行反馈、物体和设备状态变化，并将其转换为证据关联的样本，用于记忆问答和具身任务规划。我们进一步提出了ObsMem，一个观察者锚定的记忆框架，维护可见性感知的记忆和动作原生状态轨迹，以实现状态感知的决策。实验揭示了部分可观察性、被覆盖的世界状态等方面的持续挑战。
tldr: 本文提出了WorldLines基准和ObsMem记忆框架，用于评估和建模具身智能体在长期家庭任务中的记忆与状态感知能力，并揭示了部分可观察性和状态覆盖等关键挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the WorldLines benchmark and ObsMem memory framework to evaluate and model embodied agents' memory and state-awareness in long-horizon household tasks, revealing key challenges in partial observability and state overwriting.
